title: Don’t Go Back to Your Old Life — Luke 5:11
paragraphs: Don’t Go Back to Your Old Life — Luke 5:11
They dragged the boats to shore.
And then they walked away from everything.

Not because life got easier.
Not because the sea stopped calling.
But because once you’ve heard the voice of Jesus, your old life starts sounding small.
“So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed him.” — Luke 5:11

Peter knew those nets.
That water.
That routine.
That version of himself.

It was familiar.
Profitable sometimes.
Safe in a broken kind of way.
But Jesus stepped into his ordinary life and shattered the old script.
And that’s where many of us are losing the battle.

We want the miracle.
We want the blessing.
We want the full boat.
But we still keep one hand on the net.

We still leave a door cracked open for the old life.
The old relationship.
The old addiction.
The old mindset.
The old secret sin.
The old identity that Jesus already called out of us.
But here’s what we miss:
You cannot follow Christ faithfully while flirting with the life He told you to leave behind.

The call of Jesus is not renovation.
It is surrender.

He does not just improve your old life.
He gives you a new one.

Yes, the old life may still whisper.
Yes, Egypt always looks attractive when the wilderness gets hard.
Yes, the flesh loves familiar chains.
But the grace of God is stronger than your history.

Jesus did not save you so you could keep visiting the grave He pulled you out of.
He saved you to follow Him.
Fully.
Freely.
Without looking back.

So don’t go back to what almost destroyed you.
Don’t return to the version of you that existed before obedience.
Don’t trade calling for comfort.
Leave the nets.
Leave the shore.
Leave the old name.
And follow the One who still rewrites sinners into disciples.

There is hope for you in Christ.
Real hope.
Not in willpower.
Not in self-reinvention.
But in the mercy of Jesus, who calls broken people, cleans them, and leads them into new life.
Don’t go back. Jesus is ahead of you.
